column3: Close to the Greek; NKJV takes “the one coming down” as personal (“He who comes”), which the Greek allows.
NKJV has “the will of the Father who sent Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the will of Him who sent Me.”
NKJV has “the will of Him who sent Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the will of My Father.”
NKJV includes “in Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “he who believes has everlasting life.”
NKJV includes “which I shall give” a second time, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the bread … is My flesh, for the life of the world.”
NKJV includes “your” and “the manna,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “as the fathers ate and died.”
Close to the Greek; “hear” is rendered “understand.”
